allow_large: Owner approved fewer repeated lookups (2026-10-06): it touches command-line internals to look git facts up once per command, keeping every command, option and help text unchanged
done_when: Within one forge command the default branch, landed ref and git common folder are looked up once, and close reads the commits it needs with one git log call; behaviour is unchanged; a command test counts git calls in one close and shows each of those lookups happens once; the sdk_data test fixture finds the real uv even when a stub uv is on PATH; new and earlier-adopted client repos get it, with a command test for each

findings.body: Closing an existing review created by an earlier release still executes multiple worker-history logs. In src/forge/close.py:109–112, a review without `branch_diff` fingerprints HEAD and then the previously reviewed commit before `_merge_default`. Those fingerprints now call `commit_log`; the saved bookkeeping commit means the two heads differ. The fetch then deletes both cached histories here, so the fingerprint at close.py:127 issues another log—even when fetching and merging change nothing. This produces three worker-history log calls instead of one. The new count test starts an unreviewed fix in both client cases, so it passes while this upgrade path violates the budget. Extend the budget check to the legacy-review scenario already exercised by tests/test_close_keeps_reviews_for_unchanged_branch_diffs.py:123–137, and batch/reuse the history needed before and after the merge.
